newsitem.title: CHINA: Irregularities found in trade in four China stocks.
newsitem.headline: Irregularities found in trade in four China stocks.

text.p: The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges have found trading irregularities in four domestic A shares firms suspended last Friday afternoon, the exchanges said on Monday.

The statement by the Shanghai exchange said initial investigations had found some institutions using the accounts of individuals to trade in shares in Shenyang Neu-Alpine Software Co and Hebei Weiyuan Industry Co.

Investigations had also found that some individuals and institutions exceeded the exchange limits on the proportion of shares held in the two firms and that some illegal funds had been used to trade the shares, the statement said.
The exchange had decided to freeze the accounts of the institutions and individuals concerned pending further investigations, the statement said.
The Shenzhen exchange statement said probes had found illegal accounts opened for trading in Shenzhen Energy Investment Co and Luzhou Old Cellar Co.

The exchange is conducting further investigations and has ordered two unnamed securities offices, which had traded heavily in the shares of the two firms, to report their transactions to the bourse, the Shenzhen statement said.
Trading in the four firms would resume this morning, the statements said.
On Friday the two exchanges announced the suspension of trading in the four firms' shares for that afternoon, saying their share prices had moved "in an abnormal way" over the previous few days.
